newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat ends mixed, soy underscores late gains.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat ends mixed, soy underscores late gains.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures closed mixed with nearby contracts higher on speculative short covering tied to a fund-related rally in soybeans, traders said.

Fund buying in soybeans was estimated at a huge 50 million bushels, with Prudential Securities tapped for about one fifth of the tally or roughly 10 million bushels and most of the soy was purchased during the final 75 minutes of dealings.
Volume in wheat was muted amid the conflicting signals.
The market was pressured by a Sparks Companies estimate for 1997 U.S. wheat production at 2.44 billion bushels, above a USDA outlook for 2.27 billion bushels, traders said.
A Sparks Companies official revealed the firm's wheat production estimate Tuesday at the USDA's Agricultural Outlook Conference in Washington.
Talk of heavy deliveries on Friday, first notice day for the March contract, also weighed on the market, they said.
"All of the registered wheat will be delivered," a trader said.
As of early Tuesday, wheat registrations in Toledo totaled nearly 2.5 million bushels and 20,000 bushels in Chicago.
Wheat closed 3-1/4 cents per bushel higher to 5-1/2 lower, with March up two at $3.77.
Traders said wheat futures also were hit by a hike in the outlook for Australia's wheat output.
The Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics said it revised its production outlook to 23.497 million tonnes, above the previous outlook for 23.116 million.

Traders said the wheat market also was pressured by remnants of the rain and snow received over the past week in key U.S. winter wheat growing areas. New crop July Tuesday lost three cents per bushel in its spread or relationship with the nearby March contract.

Refco Inc sold nearly two million bushels of July, LIT America sold 1.5 million bushels of July and SAK Futures sold one million July, traders said. Lehman Bros bought two million bushels of July and Smith Barney bought 1.5 million bushels of July, traders said.
Technicians cited first support in the March at $3.70 per bushel and second support at $3.60. The session low was $3.68 in the March contract.
First resistance was at $3.80 and second resistance was at $3.90. The session high was $3.78.
The four- and 20-day moving averages were giving off bullish signals early Tuesday.
The short term nine-day relative strength index for the March closed at 67 percent. The market views an RSI of 70 or more as an overbought market and 30 or less as oversold.
Wheat futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 30,000 contracts, below the 35,976 traded Monday.
Wheat options trading featured Tenco Inc with a sale of 200 July $3.90 calls at 11 cents and a sale of 200 September $4.10 calls at nine cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 7,500 contracts, below the 8,078 traded Monday.
